TOW TRUCKS - TAKING THE INSURANCE INDUSTRY FOR A RIDE

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
dodgy tow truck companies are cutting road safety corners and committing serious fraud... we catch them red handed!

Summary:
TOW TRUCKING = DODGY BUSINESS!What's new? This con!

Unroadworthy trucks get a quick "make-over" to fool insurance assessors to approve accident claims - guaranteeing the transporter is covered and the dodgy tow truck company scores a deal pocketing a nice fat some of money!


Further information:
Transport Minister Dipuo Peters is pushing to now make the truck owners responsible for accidents involving trucks - bringing not only the driver to book, but also the real culprits behind unroadworthy trucks - the truck owners! But until then, truck owners are still going to cut corners when it comes to road safety - especially if there are dodgy tow truckers offering them a get out of jail free card when it comes to accidents involving unroadworthy trucks.

HOW DOES THE CON WORK?
Insurance companies won't pay out if trucks aren't in tip top shape. Dodgy tow truck companies know this and offer a special kind of add-on service for unscrupulous transporters. They will fix up your truck's roadworthy issues before the insurance assessor comes to see the truck - that way the claim will be authorised and the insurance payout secured. They tow truck crooks simply add on the fixing fee to the amount claimed for towing - cheating the insurance company, and allowing unscrupulous transporters to continue running unroadworthy trucks by offering them a get out of jail free card.

HOW BIG A PROBLEM IS IT?
85% of consumers goods is transported by road freight - the total value of goods is R450 billion annually. The long and the short of it - there are a lot of trucks on the roads - and sadly most of them are not roadworthy. In a spot check last year, 67% of truck pulled over were unroadworthiness - brake failure and bald tyres are biggest factors.

HOW DO WE DO THIS STORY?
We are going to stage an accident on a farm road. We will tip a truck on it's side. Change the breaks and tyres so that it is unroadworthy. Set up hidden cameras and call in 5 tow truck companies that will come in and "assess" the truck. We will let them tow the truck - and then bust them at their yard.

WHY DO WE CARE ABOUT THIS STORY?
Not only is it a story with cool crook and a sexy sting :) Every year thousands of people loose their lives on our roads.The International Transport Forum's (ITF) latest Road Safety Annual Report, released in November 2014, ranked South Africa the worst, out of 36 others, when it came to the number of road fatalities. It's believed that our national road death toll numbers are flawed and that the totals are actually much higher because these stats rely on police reports and often don't take into account the deaths that occur in hospital away from the accident scene. AND dodgy insurance claims push up premiums and of course that in turn pushes up prices on the shelves.

THE COST OF ROAD ACCIDENTS The report also estimated economic cost of South Africa's road crashes is estimated to be R307-billion each year – that's more than what Transnet has budgeted to fund its ambitious seven-year infrastructure build programme.


INTERVIEWS: PATRICK O'LEARY - TRUCK CHECK
CRAIG PROCTOR-PARKER - ACCIDENT SPECIALIST
UNDERCOVER STINGS
CONFRONTATIONS

Extra Budget Items:
It could be lovely to have the presenter there for the set up of the sting - while the truck is being tipped and the brakes and tyres changed. It would mean two Durban trips for the presenter. I will drive down at my own cost.

Press Release:


Insurers Taken for a Ride
South Africa sees at least 12 serious truck accidents daily, which is no surprise when considering that a whopping 67% of trucks on our roads are not roadworthy. But, how do damaged, un-roadworthy trucks get the thumbs up from insurance assessors after an accident? In one of Carte Blanche’s biggest stings yet we expose tow trucking companies offering quick-fix truck “make-overs” that fool insurance assessors into approving accident claims.


Script:


TRUCKING RECOVERY FRAUD

VO In 2013 South Africa’s road safety ranked the worst out of 36 countries - with around 12 truck accidents every day.

PATRICK: // we are killing people and no one is doing anything real to change the situation –it’s a disaster – we’re the worst in the world.

LINK: The long and the short of it is – there are a lot of trucks on the road – most of them unroadworthy - putting lives at risk.

VO: The industry is riddled with dodgy operators taking road safety short cuts says Trucking magazine editor, Patrick O’leary.

PATRICK: 67 % of the trucks on South Africa’s roads are unroadworthy, some with no brakes, some with horrendous faults.

VO: BUT how are they getting away with it?

IN 2013 we exposed how wrecks were being roadworthied for a fee….

Now it seems dodgy transporters are going a more sinister route. Willem, not his real name, is a tow truck operator with 25 years on the job – he says the biggest cover-ups start at the accident scenes.

SNITCH: //towing companies are assisting the transporters in repairing the vehicles before the assessors get to see it – // but it’s very difficult to prove that it was tampered

VO: Up for the challenge, Carte Blanche decided to test this theory in one of our biggest stings yet.

We set out to stage a truck accident.

The N3 between Johannesburg and Durban is notorious for big truck collisions – like the 2013 Pinetown Crash that claimed 23 lives.

Important to stay under the radar and not to affect traffic - we chose a quiet farm road close to the N3 freeway in the KZN Midlands.

LINK: This is our sting truck – let’s call her Delilah, at 8 tons she is a big girl. Because she’s been around the block she isn’t in the best condition – today Delilah is going to have an accident.

VO: With the help of accident scene specialists we flipped our truck, we used worn tyres and removed the brake linings on one of the back wheels.

Laurie Merchant is a brake expert and accident assessor with over 35 years experience.

LAURIE: there are no brakes on this wheel whatsoever – The insurance company would repudiate it immediately
DEVI: Like that?
LAURIE Like that – there’s no test that you can do to prove that there aren’t - there just aren’t – there’ll be no breaking on this wheel.

LINK: Delilah is now in a rather tricky position – after an accident, a tow truck will arrive and take her off – an insurance assessor will arrive and discover that she is not roadworthy and your insurance will not pay out – unless you have a friendly tow truck operator who is willing to help you.

VO: We called four local towing companies for on site quotes… one declined to come out, while another tried to sweeten the deal before even arriving.

JES TOWING: What I’m saying is I can do it for R7500, we claim R10k and I give you R2500 back, you know.

VO: Rajen in a Jes’ Towing truck was the first on the scene to respond to Delilah – without any prompting – he offered to help fix her up straight away.

RAJEN: The tyres are passable, but if you want you can swap them before the assessor comes.

VO: As he walked around Delilah, her roadworthiness became more of an issue.

RAJAN: you see like this one has a flat spot here – they can blame that – this one is fine, but this one you much change it.

PRODUCER: how do I pay for that?
RAJEN: we can try and add it on to the bill.

VO: Next to arrive was Eric from Gerry’s Towing.

ERIC: there is no brake linings here.
PRODUCER: Ok so, what does that mean?
ERIC: it needs brake linings before your assessor comes and checks it.

VO: Eric was full of solutions – even the cost for this added service could be taken care of.

ERIC: We can always work it into the price the quote for the recovery and the towing. There are lots of ways of skinning the cat.

ERIC: We’ll at night take that drum off and fit and make sure it brake.
PRODUCER: not the first time?
ERIC: We do it all the time for lots of people.


VO: Most insurance companies have a limit for towing and recovery costs – Tow Truck Insider Willem – says recovery companies know it and take full advantage – charging the max.

SNITCH: //the guys would just go crazy and bill the whole full bill //
They do all sorts of things, they put call out, travelling, labour, clean up , oil, cleanup diesel, move debris, service van, dumping of stuff and half of the time it was not done

VO: A third company arrived, with their recovery vehicle but they weren’t able to give us a quote there and then

So we turned to our two on-site offers:

Gerry’s Towing came in at R5500 + VAT: The deal included recovery, towing to their yard, changing a dodgy tyre and putting in brake linings – all before the assessor arrives.

Jes Towing came in even cheaper at just R5000: Their deal matched all the value add services Gerry’s offered – BUT, in addition they would throw in a cash kick back for the truck owner.

SNITCH: it’s not surprising to tell you honestly – because business is tough out there

VO: Our sting operation uncovered a type of fraud that the industry is unaware of says Patrick O’leary.

PATRICK: I am totally surprised, you’ve shocked me. That guys in that arena would go that route, I think it’s totally criminal

VO: Insurance assessors should pick up this fraud – Aldo Botha is from the Institute of Motor Assessors SA – he admits that they’re not aware of it either.

ALDO: We only get there once it’s done….. you’re unaware of.

VO: The scenario we staged is not so far-fetched – last year a truck operating without brake shoes brought a Johannesburg freeway to a standstill.

PATRICK: // it happened on the N12 in Alberton where one truck ran in to 47 cars, killed three people and injured countless numbers // and that truck had absolutely no brakes, I inspected the truck, the drum had no brakes inside it. So your simulated situation actually happens in reality

VO: Back at our staged accident - we went with the sweetest deal… Jes Towing got the job.

UPSOUND: Jes Towing recovery

VO: Owner Shiven came to do the recovery himself.

PRODUCER: Do you have to fix up for lot of them
SHIVEN: a lot
PRODUCER: so the insurance assessor won’t know?
SHIVEN: no, they won’t pick up anything..

VO: Aldo feels the tow truck industry needs to be regulated.

ALDO: I don’t think you’ll stamp it out completely, but if you get to a point where you’re regulating a guy and giving him a licence to operate qualification – the minute you suspect him of something you can withdraw his licence //

VO: But the reality is until then dodgy tow truck operators offer unscrupulous transporters a get out of jail free card by enabling them to sidestep road safety regulations.

Experts feel it’s the operators that should be liable for not maintaining their trucks.

PATRICK: // there is provision in the law to make them responsible and hold them responsible, but it has never been done,
LAURIE: We’ve got all the rules and regulations in the road traffic act, SABS regulations, etc, but nobody polices the regulations

VO: Jes Towing had some explaining to do – Shiven was in the workshop.

DEVI: Is that the truck you picked up?
SHIVEN: Yes
DEVI: Did you change anything?
SHIVEN: No, nothing.

VO: But when our operative visited the yard just an hour earlier – Shiven’s workers were getting their hands dirty.

MECHANIC: We are waiting for spares?
PRODUCER: What are you waiting for?
MECHANIC: The linings

DEVI: you didn’t change it?
SHIVEN; You see any there?
DEVI; you tell me you never changed it?
SHIVEN: I never touch nothing, I didn’t change the brake lining.

VO: Shiven seems to have forgotten that he was also there with his workers and our operative.

SHIVEN: as soon as I’m done I’ll let you know –
PRODUCER: half an hour?
SHIVEN: The next half an hour.
PRODUCER: It’s a second hand one to look real?
SHIVEN: Not really second hand – it’s a refurbished one – we grind it to make it look

VO: It’s seems the truth is that he not only ran out of parts, but time too. Shiven then blamed Rajan.

DEVI: An arrangement was made at that point that it was going to be included.
SHIVEN: I told no… an arrangement between him and her. I spoke to her only when I towed the truck – not when it became brake linings as things….

VO: Again a very short memory.

PRODUER: He said you put one thing?
SHIVEN: yah, the linings.

VO: We asked him about the cash kickback he offered our operative.

SHIVEN; the insurance company pays up to 10 000 for towing – we’ll charge them 7500 and we’ll give you 2500
DEVI; But that’s fraud
SHIVEN” it’s not fraud…

VO: His lawyer arrived, advising Shiven not comment any further…

After paying for the recovery of Delilah, our truck was eventually released.

Next stop – Gerry’s Towing. Owner Peter was adamant that he had no idea what was going on despite Eric calling him from the scene of the accident.

UPSOUND: if the truck gets to our yard, we need to stick brake linings in there.

VO: We refreshed his memory with the footage.

GERRY’s TOWING
PETER: He did tell me the whole story about the linings and all that
DEVI: Twice and at the end he did say it worked into the quote
PETER: He asked me to do it and the price is for whatever I gave.

VO: Peter insists that price was just for towing and that Eric lied to our operative.

PETER: I’ve got to take it up with Eric – as far as I’m concerned I run an ethical business.

VO: We also took it up with Eric.

UPSOUND CALL:
ERIC: People say anything to get a commission
DEVI: So you’re saying you lied?
ERIC: I did what?
DEVI: You lied
CUTS CALL…

VO: While Peter maintains his innocence, he still acknowledges that the industry is rotten.

PETER: I think you’re only at the tip of the iceberg – from the recovery to panel beaters to the assessors getting involved
PATRICK: – it just exacerbates the whole situation and we don’t get anywhere, we just add to the body count.


PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: In our biggest sting yet – Carte Blanche catches out dodgy tow truck operators.

SHIVEN; You see any there?
DEVI; you tell me you never changed it?
SHIVEN: I never touch nothing, I didn’t change the brake lining.


PROMO 2 15 sec
SNITCH: //towing companies are assisting the transporters in repairing the vehicles before the assessors get to see it .

VO: Carte Blanche pulls off our biggest sting yet putting tow truck operators to the test.

PROMO 3
VO: Dodgy tow truck companies help crooked transporters cut road safety corners.

RAJEN: The tyres are passable, but if you want you can swap them before the assessor comes.

VO: Carte Blanche catches them out.

MECHANIC: The linings DEVI: you didn’t change it? SHIVEN; You see any there? DEVI; you tell me you never changed it? SHIVEN: I never touch nothing, I didn’t change the brake lining. VO: Shiven seems to have forgotten that he was also there with his workers and our operative. SHIVEN: as soon as I’m done I’ll let you know – PRODUCER: half an hour? SHIVEN: The next half an hour. PRODUCER: It’s a second hand one to look real? SHIVEN: Not really second hand – it’s a refurbished one – we grind it to make it look VO: It’s seems the truth is that he not only ran out of parts, but time too. Shiven then blamed Rajan. DEVI: An arrangement was made at that point that it was going to be included. SHIVEN: I told no… an arrangement between him and her. I spoke to her only when I towed the truck – not when it became brake linings as things…. VO: Again a very short memory. PRODUER: He said you put one thing? SHIVEN: yah, the linings. VO: We asked him about the cash kickback he offered our operative. SHIVEN; the insurance company pays up to 10 000 for towing – we’ll charge them 7500 and we’ll give you 2500 DEVI; But that’s fraud SHIVEN” it’s not fraud… VO: His lawyer arrived, advising Shiven not comment any further… After paying for the recovery of Delilah, our truck was eventually released. Next stop – Gerry’s Towing. Owner Peter was adamant that he had no idea what was going on despite Eric calling him from the scene of the accident. UPSOUND: if the truck gets to our yard, we need to stick brake linings in there. VO: We refreshed his memory with the footage. GERRY’s TOWING PETER: He did tell me the whole story about the linings and all that DEVI: Twice and at the end he did say it worked into the quote PETER: He asked me to do it and the price is for whatever I gave. VO: Peter insists that price was just for towing and that Eric lied to our operative. PETER: I’ve got to take it up with Eric – as far as I’m concerned I run an ethical business. VO: We also took it up with Eric. UPSOUND CALL: ERIC: People say anything to get a commission DEVI: So you’re saying you lied? ERIC: I did what? DEVI: You lied CUTS CALL… VO: While Peter maintains his innocence, he still acknowledges that the industry is rotten. PETER: I think you’re only at the tip of the iceberg – from the recovery to panel beaters to the assessors getting involved PATRICK: – it just exacerbates the whole situation and we don’t get anywhere, we just add to the body count. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): dodgy tow truck companies are cutting road safety corners and committing serious fraud... we catch them red handed!
metadata.Summary: TOW TRUCKING = DODGY BUSINESS!What's new? This con! Unroadworthy trucks get a quick "make-over" to fool insurance assessors to approve accident claims - guaranteeing the transporter is covered and the dodgy tow truck company scores a deal pocketing a nice fat some of money!
metadata.Further information: Transport Minister Dipuo Peters is pushing to now make the truck owners responsible for accidents involving trucks - bringing not only the driver to book, but also the real culprits behind unroadworthy trucks - the truck owners! But until then, truck owners are still going to cut corners when it comes to road safety - especially if there are dodgy tow truckers offering them a get out of jail free card when it comes to accidents involving unroadworthy trucks. HOW DOES THE CON WORK? Insurance companies won't pay out if trucks aren't in tip top shape. Dodgy tow truck companies know this and offer a special kind of add-on service for unscrupulous transporters. They will fix up your truck's roadworthy issues before the insurance assessor comes to see the truck - that way the claim will be authorised and the insurance payout secured. They tow truck crooks simply add on the fixing fee to the amount claimed for towing - cheating the insurance company, and allowing unscrupulous transporters to continue running unroadworthy trucks by offering them a get out of jail free card. HOW BIG A PROBLEM IS IT? 85% of consumers goods is transported by road freight - the total value of goods is R450 billion annually. The long and the short of it - there are a lot of trucks on the roads - and sadly most of them are not roadworthy. In a spot check last year, 67% of truck pulled over were unroadworthiness - brake failure and bald tyres are biggest factors. HOW DO WE DO THIS STORY? We are going to stage an accident on a farm road. We will tip a truck on it's side. Change the breaks and tyres so that it is unroadworthy. Set up hidden cameras and call in 5 tow truck companies that will come in and "assess" the truck. We will let them tow the truck - and then bust them at their yard. WHY DO WE CARE ABOUT THIS STORY? Not only is it a story with cool crook and a sexy sting :) Every year thousands of people loose their lives on our roads.The International Transport Forum's (ITF) latest Road Safety Annual Report, released in November 2014, ranked South Africa the worst, out of 36 others, when it came to the number of road fatalities. It's believed that our national road death toll numbers are flawed and that the totals are actually much higher because these stats rely on police reports and often don't take into account the deaths that occur in hospital away from the accident scene. AND dodgy insurance claims push up premiums and of course that in turn pushes up prices on the shelves. THE COST OF ROAD ACCIDENTS The report also estimated economic cost of South Africa's road crashes is estimated to be R307-billion each year – that's more than what Transnet has budgeted to fund its ambitious seven-year infrastructure build programme.
